reason: Warm-condition signals reach the skin vessels, whose muscular walls can change their opening and affect heat loss.
expectation: The vessels should widen, bringing more blood near the surface to release heat.

effect: The warm signal widens skin vessels, increasing heat transfer to the cooler surroundings; I can now pursue the sweat response.
reaction: The heat arrows make the direction of transfer clear.
reason: Warm-condition signals also reach the sweat glands, which can help cool the body.
expectation: The glands should produce sweat for evaporative cooling.

effect: The warm signal produces liquid sweat; evaporation into the surrounding air is still needed for cooling.
reaction: The distinction between sweat production and evaporation is clear.
reason: Air at the skin provides the surroundings into which the sweat can evaporate.
expectation: Sweat should evaporate into the air, carrying heat away from the skin.

effect: Evaporation completes the warming response, and humid air reduces evaporation. I will now build the cold response.
reaction: The distinction between liquid sweat and evaporative cooling was useful.
reason: Cold-condition signals reach skin vessels, whose muscular walls can narrow to reduce heat loss.
expectation: The skin vessels should constrict, reducing blood flow near the surface and heat loss.

effect: Cold signals narrow skin vessels, reducing heat loss without producing new heat; I will try the muscle response next.
reaction: The distinction between conserving and producing heat is clear.
reason: Cold-condition signals also reach skeletal motor pathways, suggesting a shivering response.
expectation: Muscle activity should produce heat and help oppose cooling.

effect: Shivering uses ATP and produces heat, complementing the reduced heat loss from narrowed skin vessels; both temperature goals are complete.
reaction: The contrast between producing heat and conserving it was clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Evaporating sweat was most worthwhile: the picture plan distinguishes liquid sweat from cooling and shows how humid air reduces evaporation.

leastWorthwhile.text: Producing sweat was a predictable intermediate step, though it made the later evaporation distinction useful.

surprise.text: The humid-air comparison added a useful qualification: sweating does not cool as effectively when less water evaporates.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; the signals and physical roles of the available parts gave each combination a clear purpose.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue: comparing heat loss, conservation and production made the constructions informative, although the combinations were mostly predictable.
